title: Birth of Bhimrao Ramji Ambedkar at Mhow
description: Born into a Mahar family at the military cantonment of Mhow (Central Provinces), the fourteenth child of Subedar Ramji Maloji Sakpal and Bhimabai.
evidence_text: Babasaheb Dr. B.R. Ambedkar was born on 14th April 1891 at Mhow.

title: Enrollment at Columbia University, New York
description: Awarded a Baroda State Scholarship by Maharaja Sayajirao Gaekwad III, arriving in New York to commence postgraduate studies in economics, sociology, and philosophy under John Dewey and Edwin Seligman.
evidence_text: Ambedkar arrived in New York in July 1913, studying at Columbia University until 1916.

title: Presentation of 'Castes in India' Paper
description: Delivered his foundational sociological paper 'Castes in India: Their Mechanism, Genesis and Development' before Dr. Alexander Goldenweiser's Anthropology Seminar.
evidence_text: Their Mechanism, Genesis and Development Paper read before the Anthropology Seminar, 9 May 1916.

title: Launch of Mooknayak Fortnightly
description: Founded the Marathi journal 'Mooknayak' (Leader of the Silent) in Bombay with financial assistance from Chhatrapati Shahu Maharaj of Kolhapur to voice the plight of the untouchables.
evidence_text: Mooknayak was founded by Dr. Ambedkar on 31 January 1920.

title: Completion of D.Sc. at London School of Economics
description: Awarded Doctor of Science in Economics by the University of London for his monumental treatise 'The Problem of the Rupee: Its Origin and Its Solution' and called to the Bar at Gray's Inn.
evidence_text: The thesis 'The Problem of the Rupee' was accepted by the University of London for the D.Sc. in 1923.

title: Establishment of Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha
description: Formed the Depressed Classes Institute at Damodar Hall, Parel with the foundational motto: 'Educate, Agitate, Organise' to promote civic rights and socio-economic advancement.
evidence_text: Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha in Bombay was declared to organize the satyagraha struggle for human rights.

title: The Mahad Satyagraha for Water Rights
description: Led thousands of delegates at the Kolaba District Depressed Classes Conference to the public Chhadar Tank in Mahad to drink water, asserting human rights over traditional caste prohibitions.
evidence_text: The Mahad Satyagraha took place on 20 March 1927 to assert the right to water at Chhadar Tank.

title: Manusmriti Dahan Din (Burning of the Code)
description: At the second Mahad conference, Dr. Ambedkar and his co-workers publicly burned the Manusmriti on a funeral pyre, declaring it a symbol of institutionalized inequality and religious servitude.
evidence_text: On 25 December 1927 at Mahad, the Manusmriti was burned.

title: Launch of Kalaram Temple Satyagraha
description: Led non-violent protest in Nashik demanding entry of untouchables into the Kalaram Temple, demonstrating that the struggle was for equal social dignity rather than idol worship.
evidence_text: The Kalaram Temple Satyagraha in Nashik commenced in March 1930.

title: First Round Table Conference in London
description: Appointed by the Viceroy to represent the Depressed Classes in London, demanding separate electorates, fundamental rights, and equal citizenship in independent India.
evidence_text: Round Table Conference proceedings in London from 1930 to 1932.

title: Signing of the Historic Poona Pact
description: Signed between Dr. Ambedkar and caste Hindu representatives at Yerwada Central Jail following Mahatma Gandhi's fast unto death, replacing separate electorates with 148 reserved legislative seats.
evidence_text: The agreement known as the Poona Pact was signed on 24 September 1932.

title: Publication of 'Annihilation of Caste'
description: Published his masterpiece monograph in Bombay after his presidential invitation to the Lahore conference was canceled by the organizers over his critique of the Vedas.
evidence_text: Annihilation of Caste was published by Dr. Ambedkar in May 1936.

title: Election as Chairman of the Drafting Committee
description: Unanimously elected by the Constituent Assembly Drafting Committee to prepare the draft constitution of the sovereign Republic of India.
evidence_text: Dr. Ambedkar was appointed Chairman of the Drafting Committee on 29 August 1947.

title: Adoption of the Constitution of India
description: Delivered his final warning speech to the Constituent Assembly declaring that political democracy must be undergirded by social democracy, followed by the formal adoption of the Constitution.
evidence_text: The Constitution of India was formally passed and adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 26 November 1949.

title: The Historic Conversion to Buddhism at Deekshabhoomi
description: Embraced Buddhism at Nagpur with 22 vows administered to over 500,000 followers, inaugurating the modern Buddhist revival movement in India.
evidence_text: Mass conversion to Buddhism was solemnized on 14 October 1956 at Nagpur.
